result_text:
The rate limiters now use Strava's read-rate-limit headers for GET requests. I haven't run the tests or any code, so this is untested.

- **`protocol.py`:** the rate limiter is now called with the HTTP method as well as the response headers, i.e. `rate_limiter(headers, method)`.
- **`util/limiter.py`:**
  - `get_rates_from_response_headers` takes a `method` argument. For GET requests, if both `X-ReadRateLimit-Usage` and `X-ReadRateLimit-Limit` are present, it uses those. For other methods, or when the read headers are missing, it falls back to `X-RateLimit-*`.
  - `XRateLimitRule`, `SleepingRateLimitRule` and `RateLimiter` accept the method and pass it along. `method` defaults to `"GET"`, so existing callers still work.
  - `RateLimitRule` (the timer-based rule) accepts the new `method` argument but ignores it.

I did not redesign the limiter to track separate overall and read limits at the same time. For each response it picks a single set of headers to enforce, based on the method. Strava hasn't said when it will start enforcing the new limits, so I kept the change small.

Custom rate limiter callables passed to `Client` must now accept the method as a second argument, since `protocol.py` always passes it.
